annotations.text:
Two questions, one canvas.

Panning moved from Shift to Space so that Shift could go back to constraining shapes — but nothing in the editor says so, and a keystroke nobody knows about is the same as a keystroke that does not exist.

Shipped: B + C for the hint, and D as-is for the icon.

Separately: the store icon is a tray with a downward arrow in it, which is the download glyph. At 16px the shoulders drop out and only the arrow is left, so in a Chrome toolbar it sits two slots from the real download button and looks like a second one.

Everything here is drawn on the shipped tokens — Space Grotesk / JetBrains Mono, #FF4F00 on #FFFEFB, radii 6/12, the existing .hint, kbd, .label and toast styles — so none of the three needs a new component. Flip the Space held switch above the artboard to see which of them react to the key: only C does, which is the whole of its argument.

The 16px row is the one to judge on. That is the size the icon actually lives at, and it is the size where the current mark fails hardest — a downward arrow next to a downward arrow.

Whichever direction wins, the small size wants its own drawing rather than a shrunk copy of the large one; each candidate here already carries a simplified 16px form, the way the shipped set does.

The bottom block answers the follow-up question — what happens on a machine that has both tools installed.
